steps: Open the unit at Understand.
Advance to the named state or choose the reviewed changed case.
Compare activeEdgeIndexes with activeNodeIds in the bound model.
Observe that at least one focused relation names an endpoint the state does not activate; the generic map nevertheless highlights that endpoint because selected edges override state focus.
findings.observed: 51 active-edge occurrences in 36 models omit one or both endpoints from activeNodeIds.
findings.expected: Every active edge in a state has both endpoints active, so the caption, statuses, and selected relation describe one coherent state.
findings.recommendation: For each listed occurrence, either add the missing endpoint with a concrete status or remove the edge index. Recheck changed-case states first; most violations are there.

findings.title: The Domain 1.2 prediction does not answer its transit-integrity case
steps: Open d1-o02-security-concepts at Understand.
Read the scenario: altered public-transit arrival times with no sensitive data.
Open Predict and inspect all three options.
findings.observed: No option identifies integrity or frames a measurable integrity requirement for the transit page. The two distractors discuss a business feed/publisher, which belongs to the transfer case, while the keyed answer is only a generic method. All six figure nodes have empty conceptIds and restate abstract labels rather than the transit actors, data, alteration, consequence, threshold, and evidence.
findings.expected: One keyed option directly diagnoses integrity in the stated transit case and names a measurable integrity outcome; distractors stay in that same case.
findings.recommendation: Author the prediction around the transit status page, its publisher/update path, altered arrival data, safety consequence, acceptable error or freshness threshold, and integrity evidence. Keep the payroll publisher case only in transfer.

findings.title: The recovery-objective quantitative model has a missing RPO marker and a wrong concept binding
edges: last-recoverable-data-point --defines the actual recoverable-data age interval ending at--> interruption-reference-time
steps: Open d1-o07-business-continuity-requirements at Understand.
Read the quantitative figure and its text equivalent.
Inspect the nodes, conceptIds, and Business Impact Analysis detail.
findings.observed: Business Impact Analysis refers to an RPO Marker that does not exist. Interruption Reference Time is bound to recovery-time-objective even though it terminates the RPO look-back interval. The figure shows no numeric positions or intervals in the worked case, so its quantitative representation renders as six prose boxes with fragments such as “Disruption Start elapsed recovery target to RTO Marker.”
findings.expected: The model explicitly represents disruption time, restore time, last recoverable point, RTO, RPO, and MTD/MAD on compatible axes, with correct concept bindings and no nonexistent endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing RPO target/interval, bind interruption and last-recoverable points to recovery-point-objective, supply actual worked-case values, and write complete node/status sentences.

findings.title: The security-models case asks for Clark–Wilson but the worked figure teaches different models
edges: Lower-confidentiality subject --read denied by Bell-LaPadula--> Higher-confidentiality object
High-integrity subject --read denied by Biba--> Low-integrity object
steps: Open d3-o02-security-models at Understand.
Read the payment-release scenario requiring separate entry and approval through controlled transactions.
Compare the initial figure and prediction options with the scenario.
findings.observed: The scenario is a Clark–Wilson separation-of-duties/well-formed-transaction case, but the first three states show only Bell–LaPadula and Biba subject/object flows. There is no Clark–Wilson entity or edge, and Brewer–Nash appears only in focal prose. The keyed prediction says to select a model by its goal rather than identifying the violating action requested by the prompt.
findings.expected: The worked case contains user, transformation procedure, constrained data item, integrity verification procedure, and separated roles, and the keyed answer resolves the specific payment-release action.
findings.recommendation: Make Clark–Wilson the worked case, move Bell–LaPadula/Biba/Brewer–Nash into distinct comparison cases, and rewrite the prediction so one answer directly resolves the stated operation.

findings.title: Two sequence diagrams use six stages or artifacts as persistent lifelines
edges: d3: external upload event → API/event gate → function → classifier → store, plus deployment authority
d4: maintenance request → identity/device → jump endpoint → operation → evidence → closure
steps: Open each unit at Understand.
Inspect the rendered sequence headings and vertical lifelines.
Compare each heading with a persistent actor that can send or receive a message.
findings.observed: Both diagrams render six lifelines. Upload event, maintenance request, operation, evidence, and closure are transient stages/artifacts, so the lifelines imply persistence and message exchange the authored entities do not have. The D4 edge “Observed session and artifacts supports review and confirms the required Revocation and verified closure” is an evidence dependency, not a message.
findings.expected: Sequence uses at most five persistent actors and actual message order, or the model uses state/decision/boundary for gates and artifacts.
findings.recommendation: Convert these to state or boundary models, or replace the headings with true actors/services and keep stages as messages or state changes.

findings.title: Seven transfer visuals reuse entities from a different system
steps: Open each listed unit at Understand.
Choose Reviewed changed case or inspect changed-case state.
Compare transfer prompt nouns with node labels and active statuses.
findings.observed: The changed fact is carried almost entirely in the caption/status while the diagram remains another system: payroll policy engine over partner-upload nodes; orchestrator over edge-update nodes; SaaS public sharing over document-intake nodes; HPC scheduler over firmware/control-system nodes; hypervisor over browser/API/database nodes; redundant switches over NAC endpoint nodes; meeting recording over vendor-maintenance nodes.
findings.expected: The changed case preserves relevant entities and replaces or adds the entity whose changed fact drives the consequence.
findings.recommendation: Author variant-specific entities through a separate model where necessary, or keep the transfer within the same system boundary. A caption pasted onto unrelated boxes is not a changed-case visual.

findings.title: Boundary and ledger lanes misstate membership or declare an empty semantic region
steps: Open each listed boundary/ledger model at Understand.
Read lane labels/rules and inspect which nodes render in each lane.
Compare node role with the stated membership rule.
findings.observed: Examples visible in the release: d1-o10 leaves Origin empty and puts Partner Actor in Boundary/control; d3-o08 puts Restricted Operations Room, Approved Personnel, Emergency Egress, and People Safety in Origin while Protected side is empty; d3-o03 ledger leaves Decision subjects empty; d3-o05-platform-data-architecture and d3-o06-cryptographic-solutions leave Protected side empty. Other listed models declare similarly empty origin/protected lanes.
findings.expected: Every lane has meaningful membership and each node belongs to the lane whose rule describes that actor, control, protected resource, or evidence.
findings.recommendation: Reassign nodes based on case semantics, remove unused lanes, and add missing protected outcomes/evidence where the representation requires them.

findings.title: Visible state statuses are authored as truncated sentence fragments
steps: Open an affected unit at Understand.
Advance to Case facts or Changed fact.
Read the bold node status shown above the node detail.
findings.observed: 81 literal ellipsis strings across 32 files end before the consequence or control is complete; examples include “Treat the recording as a new governed copy ... and protect…” and “RPO ... exceeded…” patterns.
findings.expected: Each status is a short, complete, concrete outcome label; layout handles clipping rather than authored strings ending mid-thought.
findings.recommendation: Replace each listed value with a concise complete status (for example “public recording link: exposure unresolved”); keep full reasoning in captions.

findings.title: Thirteen checks cue the keyed answer by length and specificity
steps: Open the named check without revealing feedback.
Compare the three answer labels.
Note that the correct option is at least 1.40 times the mean distractor length and often is the only multi-control operational sentence.
findings.observed: The keyed answer is consistently more complete and specific than brief absolute distractors in the listed checks, enabling test-taking by form rather than concept.
findings.expected: Plausible alternatives have comparable grammatical form, scope, and specificity.
findings.recommendation: Balance option length and make distractors plausible bounded decisions that fail one precise condition.

findings.title: Twenty-four models leave assessed visual entities without concept provenance
steps: Inspect node conceptIds in the bound files.
Compare empty nodes with concepts assessed by prediction, transfer, and retry.
findings.observed: 87 nodes across 24 files have empty conceptIds; d1-o02 leaves all six empty, and d3-o01 leaves all six empty even though the checks assess named design principles.
findings.expected: Every visual entity that teaches or is assessed maps to the exact canonical concept IDs it instantiates; truly contextual actors may remain untagged only when they teach no concept.
findings.recommendation: Map each teaching/control node to the canonical concepts it actually demonstrates, and leave empty only pure case actors with an explicit rationale.

findings.title: Generated option and node prose leaks template artifacts
steps: Open affected checks and read option labels aloud.
Inspect node details in the affected generated models.
findings.observed: Labels include malformed “.; no separate scope or evidence check is needed” and template prefixes such as “Given the stated facts” / “In this case.” Many details simply concatenate node labels and edge text (“Failure Scenario is diagnosed by consequence Property Question”) rather than explain the case.
findings.expected: Options read as natural parallel decisions and node details describe the concrete case.
findings.recommendation: Edit the authored prose directly; remove template prefixes/suffixes and write complete case-specific sentences.
